Team —

I reviewed Novapay's proposed language. High level: I am open to a tightly scoped provisional-measures consent but with three guardrails:

1) The consent must be limited to "provisional, interim or conservatory measures to preserve assets or prevent imminent data exfiltration or irreparable harm" and explicitly exclude final relief or substantive merits determinations.

2) The clause should require immediate referral to the contract's dispute resolution process for any subsequent permanent relief (i.e., arbitration remains the primary forum for the merits).

3) We need a clear, operational service-of-process and notice protocol (email escalation + designated agent in Spain + 24/7 legal on-call number). That protocol must be an exhibit to the MSA and limited to provisional-measures events.

Draft language (please review):
"Notwithstanding Section [X] (Dispute Resolution), Customer may seek provisional, interim or conservatory measures in the courts of Customer's place of incorporation solely to preserve rights or prevent imminent and irreparable harm related to Customer Data. Such measures are strictly limited to interim relief and shall not determine the merits of any dispute, which shall proceed to arbitration under Section [Y]. Redwood consents to service of process for such provisional measures in the manner set forth in Exhibit Z (Service & Provisional Relief Protocol)."

Operational note: Exhibit Z should list the designated agent (name + legal@redwood.com), the DPO contact, an on-call mobile for emergencies (legal team rotation), and an acknowledgement procedure (Redwood will confirm receipt within 2 hours).

Risk flags: this will create a narrow jurisdictional exposure for interim actions in Spain; however, because we explicitly preserve arbitration for merits and limit remedy scope, exposure for longer-term litigation is minimal. If Sales needs to keep the account moving, I can approve this redline subject to Laura's final sign-off and an internal security ops runbook for responding to provisional-measures requests.

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
